skill.name: swiftui-performance-audit
skill.description: Audit SwiftUI runtime performance from code, architecture, and user-supplied profiling evidence. Use it to diagnose slow rendering, janky scrolling, high CPU or memory use, excessive view updates, and layout thrash.
skill.summary: Find and fix SwiftUI performance bottlenecks with code review and profiling guidance.
skill.author: Dimillian

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, Swift code examples, and ordinary SwiftUI performance guidance. I found no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, command execution instructions, or system reconnaissance behavior in the reviewed files.

static_findings.snippet: ## Avoid slow initialization in view bodies
- Avoid inline filtering in `ForEach`; pre-filter and cache collections.
- Avoid `AnyView` in list rows; it hides identity and increases cost.
- Avoid broad dependencies that trigger many updates (e.g., `@Observable` arrays or global environme
- Environment values update checks still cost time; avoid placing fast-changing values (timers, geom
- Avoid long-running tasks on the main dispatch queue or main actor.
- Avoid broad dependencies that fan out updates to many views.
- Avoid storing closures that capture parent state; precompute child views.
- Unstable identity in lists (`id` churn, `UUID()` per render).
- Heavy work in `body` (formatting, sorting, image decoding).

content.value_statement: SwiftUI apps can hide rendering, identity, and state update problems that cause slow screens. This skill reviews code and profiling evidence to produce focused fixes and verification steps.
actual_capabilities: Reviews SwiftUI views for excessive body work, unstable identity, and broad state dependencies.
Guides users through SwiftUI Instruments captures when code review is not enough.
Maps profiling symptoms to likely causes such as long body updates, hitches, and update fan-out.
Suggests targeted refactors for state scope, list identity, caching, image decoding, and layout complexity.
Produces prioritized findings with expected impact, effort, and re-measurement steps.
limitations: It cannot run Instruments or collect traces without user-provided profiling output.
It cannot guarantee performance gains without measuring the same scenario before and after changes.
It depends on representative code, device details, build configuration, and reproduction steps.
It focuses on SwiftUI runtime behavior, not general backend, networking, or database performance.

use_cases.title: Diagnose slow SwiftUI screens
use_cases.description: Review a problematic view and identify body work, identity, state, or layout issues that may cause delays.

use_cases.title: Interpret profiling evidence
use_cases.description: Use screenshots or notes from Instruments to connect long updates and hitches to likely code changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare a performance review
use_cases.description: Create a prioritized remediation plan before a release or after a regression appears in a feature branch.

prompt_templates.title: Review one view
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this SwiftUI view for performance issues. Focus on expensive body work, state dependencies, list identity, and layout complexity.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate scroll jank
prompt_templates.prompt: I see janky scrolling in this SwiftUI list. Review the code and suggest likely causes, fixes, and what I should measure next.

prompt_templates.title: Use Instruments evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these SwiftUI Instruments findings and Time Profiler notes. Map the evidence to root causes and propose prioritized remediation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a verification plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a before-and-after verification plan for this SwiftUI performance issue. Include metrics, capture setup, expected deltas, and risk areas.

output_examples.input: A SwiftUI feed view stutters during scrolling and creates formatters inside row bodies.
output: Top issue: formatter allocation occurs during frequent row updates.
Recommended fix: move formatting into cached helpers or precomputed display strings.
Verification: re-run the same scroll capture and compare long body updates and hitch count.

output_examples.input: An Instruments capture shows many frequent updates without one obvious slow body.
output: Likely cause: broad observable dependencies fan out updates across unrelated views.
Recommended fix: split state into granular view models and pass stable values into rows.
Verification: compare update counts for the same interaction after the refactor.

output_examples.input: A release candidate has higher memory and slow navigation on an image-heavy screen.
output: Likely cause: image decoding or resizing happens near the main interaction path.
Recommended fix: downsample off the main thread and cache display-ready images.
Verification: compare memory peak, navigation delay, and main-thread busy periods.

best_practices: Provide the target SwiftUI code, reproduction steps, device model, OS version, and build configuration.
Share Instruments screenshots or trace summaries when symptoms remain unclear after code review.
Re-measure the same interaction after each fix to confirm the performance change.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for broad optimization without code, symptoms, or a measurable target interaction.
Do not treat every SwiftUI update as a bug without comparing it to user-visible impact.
Do not apply many refactors at once before taking a baseline measurement.

faq.question: Does this skill run Instruments for me?
faq.answer: No. It explains what to capture and analyzes traces, screenshots, or notes that you provide.

faq.question: Can it review code without profiling data?
faq.answer: Yes. It starts with code review and asks for profiling evidence when the cause is still uncertain.

faq.question: What SwiftUI issues does it target?
faq.answer: It targets slow body updates, unstable identity, broad state dependencies, layout churn, image decoding, and scrolling hitches.

faq.question: Will it rewrite my SwiftUI feature?
faq.answer: It proposes focused code changes and refactors. Large rewrites still need project-specific engineering judgment.

faq.question: What information improves the result?
faq.answer: The best inputs include the target view, models, reproduction steps, baseline metrics, and relevant Instruments evidence.

faq.question: Can it help verify a fix?
faq.answer: Yes. It defines before-and-after metrics and asks you to re-run the same capture for comparison.
